title: DreamBench-SWE: A Multi-Session Memory-Hygiene Benchmark for Software Agents

visual_explainer.blocker: No paper-grounded mechanism figure was available; the record remains text-only rather than publishing an unverified synthesis.

analysis.tldr: DreamBench-SWE provides executable evidence that retained project state changes later patches, but its preregistered comparisons do not show that typed consolidation or sleep beats a verbatim store. The benchmark is stronger than its reference memory mechanism.
analysis.problem: Multi-session software work needs an executable test of whether earlier arbitrary project state survives, remains in scope, resolves contradictions, and changes a later patch.
analysis.core_idea: Inject non-inferable evidence in S1/S2, require it in S3, and grade the resulting repository with a hidden oracle while comparing no external memory, verbatim storage, typed/raw/hybrid reference probes, and literal-storage Mem0.

memory_design.write: The reference probe preserves immutable raw episodes and derives typed episodic, semantic, procedural, failure, feedback, constraint, contradiction, and dream records.
memory_design.organize: Sleep consolidates types, extracts failure, replays counterfactuals, repairs contradictions, and suppresses stale records.
memory_design.read: Broad retrieval is gated by status, scope, validity, supersession, risk, staleness, provenance, and type under a fixed context budget.
memory_design.update_forget: Logical forgetting suppresses stale state while raw episodes remain immutable; the later wake actor edits the repo from admitted memory.

compared_to: No external memory versus deterministic verbatim storage under the same GPT-5.5 wake task and tools
Hybrid typed/raw reference probe versus verbatim, raw-only, and typed-only probes
A matched factorial consolidation control with equal sleep compute is missing
analysis.evidence: In v2.1, no memory scores 21/180 (.1167), verbatim 82/180 (.4556), hybrid 83/180 (.4611), and Mem0 literal storage 97/180 (.5389). Persistent evidence clearly changes later executable patches, but hybrid-versus-verbatim, raw-only, and typed-only preregistered tests all fail to reject. Contradiction records appear in 0/180 hybrid/raw reads.
analysis.why_it_matters: A memory benchmark should grade later actions and expose hygiene failures, while refusing to attribute an end-to-end gain to typed organization when a matched verbatim archive performs the same.
limitations: Synthetic fixture repositories and arbitrary exact tokens dominate; 18 of 22 historical traps are recall-verbatim and favor literal storage.
Only one feasible hosted wake model remains; native Mem0 and Supermemory fail conformance, and the reference-probe ablations do not isolate its intended mechanisms.
Hybrid uses 174.205M tokens and 12,655 judge calls versus 2.209M tokens for verbatim storage; storage, production latency, service price, and energy remain incomplete.
